taxonomyNote: USGS and GeckoWeb call the species the white-spotted wall gecko; NatureServe and the batch use 'ringed wall gecko'.
fieldMarks: Large, stocky gecko, up to about 15 cm total length (USGS notes about 108 mm snout-vent).
Gray to tan back covered with rows of large rough tubercular scales; a distinctive group of four white spots on the shoulders.
White belly with shingle-like round, slightly overlapping scales; large bulging eyes with fixed transparent covering.
Undivided toepads (house geckos have divided pads).
behavior: In Florida lives on the walls of buildings; pugnacious, bites and squeaks when grabbed.
Preys on insects and smaller lizards, including house geckos; native-range clutches are 1-2 eggs, several per year.
habitat: Introduced populations are associated with buildings and urban environs; in its native North African range habitat is desert.
range: Native to northern and Saharan/sub-Saharan Africa. Introduced in the United States: Florida (known since the 1990s from scattered sites including Lee and Miami-Dade counties) and California (Redlands, San Bernardino County, since the early 2000s; San Juan Capistrano, Orange County, 2020); NatureServe lists it as non-native. Not in Canada.
